title: t1273: Add supervisor sanity-check for self-healing queue stalls
body:
## Summary

- Adds Phase 0.9 sanity check to the supervisor pulse cycle — runs when zero tasks are dispatchable but open tasks exist in TODO.md
- Cross-references DB state, TODO.md state, and system state to find contradictions that cause silent queue stalls
- Fixes Phase 0.5d to treat permanently failed blockers as resolved, preventing infinite dependency chain stalls

## Problem

The supervisor pulse was running every 2 minutes, logging "No new tasks to pick up" hundreds of times, while 13 open tasks sat idle. Three interlocking failures caused the stall:

1. **DB-failed tasks with TODO.md claims (double-lock)**: Tasks failed in DB but still had `assignee:/started:` in TODO.md. Phase 0.5e has a 24h threshold, but the DB already knows the task failed — waiting 24h is unnecessary
2. **Failed dependency chains never cascade**: When a root task fails permanently, its dependents wait forever because Phase 0.5d only checks for `[x]` or `[-]` status
3. **Missing `#auto-dispatch` tag**: Tasks with clear specs, model assignments, and estimates were invisible to auto-pickup because they lacked the tag

## Changes

### New: `.agents/scripts/supervisor/sanity-check.sh`
Phase 0.9 module with 5 checks:
- **Check 1**: Strip stale claims on DB-failed tasks immediately (DB state is authoritative)
- **Check 2**: Unblock tasks whose blockers permanently failed (retries exhausted)
- **Check 3**: Auto-tag dispatchable tasks missing `#auto-dispatch`
- **Check 4**: Cancel DB orphans with no TODO.md entry
- **Check 5**: Log structured stall breakdown when nothing is fixable

### Modified: `.agents/scripts/supervisor/pulse.sh`
- Integrates Phase 0.9 between Phase 1d (post-completion unblock) and Phase 2 (dispatch)
- Only runs when zero tasks are queued but open tasks exist
- Re-runs auto-pickup after fixes so newly dispatchable tasks enter the queue immediately

### Modified: `.agents/scripts/supervisor/todo-sync.sh`
- Phase 0.5d (`auto_unblock_resolved_tasks`) now checks if a blocker is permanently failed in DB (retries >= max_retries)
- Permanently failed blockers are treated as resolved, unblocking dependents

### Modified: `.agents/scripts/supervisor-helper.sh`
- Sources the new `sanity-check.sh` module

## Design Principle

"Don't assume, verify." Deterministic state machines make assumptions that cause silent failures. When state is contradictory, cross-reference all available data sources to resolve it rather than waiting for timeouts.

## Testing

- ShellCheck: zero violations on all 4 files
- Designed to be triggered by the current stalled queue (0 queued, 0 running, 13 open tasks)

  * Treats permanently failed blockers as resolved to prevent indefinite blocking.

title: t1275: KIRA-informed completion discipline across all autonomy levels
body:
## Summary

Based on [KIRA/terminal-bench research](https://github.com/krafton-ai/KIRA) (Kangwook Lee), adds completion discipline and behavioural corrections across all autonomy levels in the aidevops harness.

KIRA demonstrated +10 percentage point improvement on terminal-bench by addressing fundamental LLM behavioural defaults: false completion, poor self-evaluation, bad adaptive replanning, and narrow solutions. These are not terminal-specific bugs — they're training artefacts that affect every session type.

## Changes

### Layer 1: `build.txt` (universal — every session, every domain)
- New "Completion and quality discipline" section with 5 principles:
  - Drive to verified completion, don't hand off partial work
  - Self-evaluate honestly before declaring done
  - Replan when stuck, don't patch
  - Build for change, not for the moment
  - Prefer lightweight approaches

### Layer 2: `AGENTS.md` (development lifecycle)
- Structured 5-step completion self-check added to both `.agents/AGENTS.md` and root `AGENTS.md`
- Requires explicit requirement listing (DONE/TODO) before declaring any task complete

### Layer 3: `dispatch.sh` (headless worker prompt)
- New "Completion Self-Check" section with 4 mandatory checks before FULL_LOOP_COMPLETE
- New "Replan when stuck" section (item 8 in efficiency protocol)
- Updated item 7 to encourage one alternative strategy before BLOCKED

### Layer 4: `ralph-loop.md` + `full-loop.md` (loop agents)
- New section 6 in ralph-loop.md: replanning guidance with signs, triggers, and how-to
- Enhanced completion criteria in full-loop.md: generalization check, replanning rule

## Impact

- **102 lines added** across 6 files, **6 lines removed** (net +96)
- Zero structural changes — all additions are prompt text and documentation
- ShellCheck clean on dispatch.sh
- Affects all three autonomy levels: interactive, loop agents, headless workers

## Research Source

- Paper: [Kangwook Lee's KIRA analysis](https://x.com/Kangwook_Lee/status/2024781354232356946)
- Code: [krafton-ai/KIRA](https://github.com/krafton-ai/KIRA)
- Key finding: Simple prompt fixes (structured self-evaluation, replanning guidance, generalization rules) yield +10pp on frontier models

title: t1276: Subtask-aware queue analysis, fix auto-pickup head-50 limit, orphan issue intake
body:
## Summary

- **Fix auto-pickup Strategy 4 `head -50` limit** — silently skipped subtask inheritance for parents beyond the 50th position. Only 2 of 242 `#auto-dispatch` parents have open subtasks, but both were beyond position 50. Now scans only open `[ ]` parents with no arbitrary limit.
- **Enhance runners-check** — reports subtask-aware queue depth: total open (parents + subtasks), dispatchable (tagged + inherited), blocked, and claimed counts. Subtasks are the actual dispatchable work units.
- **Add TODO entries for 3 orphan user-reported GitHub issues**: GH#1791 (setup.sh unbound variable), GH#1975 (skill discovery CLI), GH#1991 (wp-helper.sh CONFIG_FILE bug)
- **Re-add completed task entries** for t1260, t1261, t1273 with `pr:` refs so issue-sync can close their stale open GitHub issues

## Root Cause

`cmd_auto_pickup()` Strategy 4 collected parent IDs with `head -50 | sort -u`. With 242 `#auto-dispatch` parents in TODO.md (mostly completed), the open parents with subtasks (t1120, t1264) were beyond position 50 and never processed. Their subtasks (t1120.1, t1120.2, t1120.4, t1264.2) were invisible to the dispatcher despite the parent having `#auto-dispatch`.

## Files Changed

- `.agents/scripts/supervisor/cron.sh` — Remove `head -50`, filter to open parents only
- `.agents/scripts/commands/runners-check.md` — Subtask-aware queue depth reporting
- `TODO.md` — 3 new tasks (t1277-t1279), 3 restored completed tasks (t1260, t1261, t1273), t1276 entry

title: t1279: Fix wp-helper.sh run_wp_command() CONFIG_FILE not propagated from get_site_config subshell
body:
## Summary

Two related bugs in `wp-helper.sh` affecting the most common code path (`run_wp_command`):

**Bug 1 — Missing `load_config` before subshell call**

`run_wp_command()` called `get_site_config()` via command substitution `$()` without first calling `load_config`. The `CONFIG_FILE` variable set inside `get_site_config`'s subshell was lost when the subshell exited, leaving `CONFIG_FILE` empty when `execute_wp_via_ssh()` → `resolve_server_ref()` tried to read it.

Fix: added `load_config` before the `get_site_config "$site_key"` call, matching the pattern already used by `run_on_category()` and `run_on_all()`.

**Bug 2 — `print_warning` stdout pollution in `resolve_server_ref()`**

`print_warning` (via `print_shared_warning`) outputs to stdout without `>&2`. When `resolve_server_ref()` emits a warning for a missing `server_ref`, the warning text was captured by the `$()` in `execute_wp_via_ssh`, prepended to the JSON, and caused downstream `jq` parse errors.

Fix: added `>&2` redirect to the `print_warning` call in `resolve_server_ref()` so the warning goes to stderr and does not pollute the captured JSON.

## Verification

- ShellCheck: zero violations (`shellcheck -x -S warning .agents/scripts/wp-helper.sh`)
- Both fixes match patterns already established in the codebase

Ref #1991

title: t1285: Fix supervisor pipeline — BSD sed, dedup suppression, adaptive pulsing
body:
## Summary

Fixes 4 interconnected issues preventing the supervisor pipeline from dispatching tasks:

- **BSD sed regex error** — `+?` lazy quantifier unsupported on macOS BSD sed, causing repo slug extraction to fail every pulse cycle (3 files fixed)
- **Bash arithmetic error** — `grep -c` returning multi-line output causing `[[: 0 0: syntax error in expression` in `has_actionable_work()`
- **Dedup suppression blocking auto-dispatch** — Two-phase `propose_auto_dispatch` flow was broken because Phase 2 (confirmation) was suppressed by dedup window (~2.5 hours). 864 total suppressions observed. Fixed with explicit bypass + state hash improvement
- **Fixed 300s AI reasoning cooldown** — Now adaptive: 60s when queued tasks exist, 600s when idle. Configurable via `SUPERVISOR_AI_COOLDOWN_ACTIVE` and `SUPERVISOR_AI_COOLDOWN_IDLE`

## Changes

| File | Fix |
|------|-----|
| `ai-reason.sh` | BSD sed fix, grep -c sanitization, adaptive cooldown |
| `ai-actions.sh` | BSD sed fix, dedup bypass for Phase 2 confirmation, `[proposed:...]` in state hash |
| `routine-scheduler.sh` | BSD sed fix |

## Testing

- ShellCheck: zero new violations on all 3 files
- BSD sed regex verified on macOS: correctly extracts `owner/repo` from SSH and HTTPS URLs with/without `.git` suffix
- Phase 0.7 stale-eval recovery confirmed working (t1120.4 already recovered to `verified`)

## Post-merge

After merge and `aidevops update`, reset stuck tasks:
```bash
sqlite3 ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/supervisor/supervisor.db \
  "UPDATE tasks SET status='queued', retries=0, error=NULL, updated_at=strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ','now') WHERE id IN ('t1158','t1267');"
```

Closes #2038
